newsitem.title: USA: LTV steel plant cited for pollution by EPA.
newsitem.headline: LTV steel plant cited for pollution by EPA.

text.p: LTV Steel Co.'s Cleveland, Ohio, plant was cited by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency for exceeding legal pollution limits, the agency said on Monday.
The LTV Corp unit was given 30 days from receipt of the notice of violation to request a meeting to discuss the allegations.
To resolve the "preliminary finding of violations," the EPA said it could issue a compliance order, assess an adminstrative penalty or bring suit against the company.

The EPA said the plant exceeded legal limits for visible emissions of particulates from two blast furnaces and a basic oxygen funace. It also exceeded legal limits for sulfur dioxide emissions, the agency said.
Air quality in the Cleveland area does not meet federal standards for particulates and sulfur dioxide, it said.
LTV recently agreed to pay $1.25 million in civil penalties and to spend another $1.8 million on a project to reduce emissions from the company's coke plant in Chicago.
